messages:
maya: :warning: Heads up — seeing a perf regression in prod after the runtime v2.14.3 deploy. Short chat requests (1-4 tokens) p50 up ~30%. Traced to kernel selector frequently falling back to the slow SDPA path for some head_dim shapes.

dev-bot: deploy-bot: runtime v2.14.3 rolled to prod @ 2026-03-16T21:52:00Z

alex: which model / head_dim distribution? any logs or a quick repro?

maya: quick excerpt from runtime logs (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-16T21:55:12Z] kernel_picker: model=custom-chat-13b head_dim=56 seq_len=8 causal=true device=sm80
[2026-03-16T21:55:12Z] kernel_probe: candidates=[flash_v3, flash_v2, sdpa_naive]
[2026-03-16T21:55:12Z] kernel_pick: chosen=sdpa_naive reason="head_dim not tile-aligned -> v3/v2 unsafe fallback"
[2026-03-16T21:55:12Z] perf: tokens=2 latency_ms=24.1

# previous baseline: 16.2ms
```

sam: ugh. headdim=56 again. We've hit this before on SM80 where tiling heuristics don't match head_dim % 8 != 0 and the autotuner pessimistically chooses naive SDPA. Also KV-cache/path sharing makes the hot path skew to seq_len<=16 which amplifies the cost.

alex: did the autotuner run on canaries for this model? maybe it picked safe kernels from historical runs.

maya: autotuner had prior data but for longer seq lengths (64+). We didn't have representative short-seq microbenchmarks for head_dim=56 on SM80, so selector favored the safe codepath when requests with seq_len<=16 started dominating.

ryan: proposals: 1) normalize head_dim for kernel scoring (round to nearest 8/16) when choosing kernels so we don't over-penalize odd dims, 2) add short-seq microbench sample to the per-model-per-device autotune pass, 3) cache kernel latencies per (machine,device,head_norm,causal_flag,seq_bucket).

alex: +1 for head_norm. Also consider a soft-priority for flash_v3 on causal when seq_len <= 32 — empirically it's often better even for non-exact tile shapes (we've been masking small extras).

maya: repro command I used locally:
```
python tools/bench_kernels.py --model custom-chat-13b --device sm80 --head-dim 56 --seq-len 8 --batch 1 --repeat 200
# sample output
# flash_v3: warmup failed (tile mismatch) -> skip
# flash_v2: 20.3 ms/op
# sdpa_naive: 23.9 ms/op (chosen by runtime)
```

sam: is correctness at risk if we force v3 despite non-aligned head_dim? or is it only a performance/edge rounding issue?

maya: correctness is fine — the fallbacks are safety from untested tiling code paths and some kernels assert on padding assumptions. But we've validated v3 for this model on SM80 in dev machines; the selector's conservative rule is the problem.

ryan: plan: I'll open a PR to autotuner to implement head_dim normalization + add a short-seq (<=32) microbench step. I'll also add a cheap canary flag (10% traffic) to prefer flash_v3 for causal routes so we can measure real-world p50/p95 impact.

alex: please include metrics to watch: p50 token latency, p95 token latency, and tail CPU spin time after evictions. Also add an automated regression alert if p50 jumps >15% within 30m of rollout.

maya: created a short perf diff run on staging showing p50 drop from 22.4ms -> 15.6ms after forcing v3 for causal small-seq. Will paste flamegraph later.

dev-bot: perf-alert: route=/chat/stream p50 increased 32% between 21:30-22:00 in prod (investigation thread: this one)

sam: small nit — make sure per-AI-candidate cache keys include causal vs non-causal and KV-cache-enabled flag; KV-cache reduces locality so kernel perf can flip.

ryan: noted. I'll include (head_norm,seq_bucket,causal,kv_enabled,device_arch) in the key. Also will add nightly job to re-benchmark top 50 models on each device arch.

maya: thanks — I'll collect the microbench traces and attach to the PR. Let's aim to ship the autotuner tweak and canary today if possible.

alex: thanks team. Keep thread updated.

ryan: I'll take it, opening PR now. :hammer_and_wrench:
